chunks: And from him, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Isma'il, from Muhammad ibn al-Fudayl, from Abu al-Subah al-Kinanī, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)
that he was asked about kissing the Ka'bah, so he said: 'From its rear.'
ai.seo_question: Where exactly should one kiss the Ka'bah during tawaf according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) clarifies the specific location for *istilam* (kissing or touching the Ka'bah), directing it to the 'rear' (*dubur*). While some scholars interpret this as the corner opposite the door, others view it as the section of the wall between the Yemeni corner and the door, highlighting the precision Shia jurisprudence applies to ritual gestures during *tawaf*.
